title: Crock Barbacoa Chicken
shortDescription: Slow-cooked chipotle chicken that shreds for tacos and bowls
subtitle: Slow-cooked chipotle chicken that shreds for tacos and bowls
description: Chicken thighs braise low with chipotle, lime, cumin, and oregano until pull-apart tender. Shred for tacos, rice bowls, or lettuce wraps.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Crock Barbacoa Chicken in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Layer crock ingredients
steps.instruction: Place onion slices in bottom of 8-quart slow cooker. Arrange chicken thighs on top in an even layer without stacking too deep. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Mix braising liquid
steps.instruction: Whisk chipotle, adobo sauce, lime juice, vinegar, cumin, oregano, garlic, salt, pepper, and broth until smooth. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Slow cook until tender
steps.instruction: Pour liquid over chicken. Cover and cook on low 6–8 hours until meat pulls apart easily and internal temp reaches 165°F throughout. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Shred in pot
steps.instruction: Transfer thighs to a cutting board if easier, or shred in crock with two forks. Meat should separate into moist strands, not dry clumps. Plan about 10 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Crock Barbacoa Chicken onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Reduce juices if needed
steps.instruction: If liquid is thin, simmer shredded chicken on high 20–30 minutes uncovered until sauce clings to meat with a glossy coat. Maintain a steady simmer — bubbles should break the surface without a rolling boil that shreds delicate proteins. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

proTips: Thighs beat breast here—long cook needs fat for tender shred.
Offer both corn tortillas and rice bowls to split crew preferences.
Freeze shredded portions in cooking liquid for fast taco nights.
tonightSpread: Warm corn tortillas and pickled red onion.
Cilantro-lime rice in a hotel pan.
leftovers: Barbacoa breakfast burritos with eggs and salsa.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Set-and-forget protein that feeds multiple formats. Smoky heat without standing over a smoker all day.
mealPrepNotes: Start crock on low by mid-morning. Shred with two forks directly in the pot to save dishes. Station: Do not lift lid during first 3 hours—each peek adds 15 minutes cook time. Station: Skim fat before shredding for cleaner flavor and easier cleanup. Station: Hold shredded chicken in juice at 165°F—dry holding ruins barbacoa texture.
